description: Curated, editable next-step heuristic for AEGIS SOC. Weights and horizons are analyst judgement for ranking attention, not measured frequencies or probabilities.
notes: Every technique ID must exist in techniques.json (verified against attack.mitre.org); loading fails otherwise.
Watch signals use the same field-condition grammar as the rule DSL: event kinds plus conditions (all must hold), or any listed rule firing on the event.
Preventive actions may reference only allowlisted simulated playbooks, which still require human approval.

actions.text: Reset the account's password and review its recent logons
Collect an evidence manifest for the asset

watch.description: Logon to this asset from an internal address

actions.text: Pivot on the account to check logons on other hosts
Consider requesting simulated isolation of the source host if lateral movement is confirmed
Block unexpected east-west connections from the host
Consider requesting simulated isolation if scanning continues
Review proxy logs for downloads from this host
Collect an evidence manifest for the asset

watch.description: Credential dumping tools or LSASS access

actions.text: Plan credential resets for accounts used on this host
Consider requesting simulated isolation if dumping is confirmed
Verify offline backups for affected systems
Consider requesting simulated isolation of the host

watch.description: Connection reported as a large upload

actions.text: Review outbound volume from this host at the proxy or firewall
Collect an evidence manifest for the asset

transitions.rationale: Password guessing is usually followed by a login with a guessed credential.
With a working session, attackers commonly run PowerShell to execute commands.
A valid account is typically used to enumerate accounts and groups before escalating.
Valid credentials are frequently reused to reach other hosts over remote services.
Scripted execution is often used to scan the internal network for reachable services.
PowerShell is a common way to download additional tools onto a compromised host.
Attackers with code execution often try to dump credentials from memory.
Discovered remote services such as SMB, RDP, SSH or WinRM are natural targets for lateral movement.
Ransomware operators spread through remote services before encrypting data.
Access to more hosts is often followed by staging and exfiltrating data.
A newly created account is typically used to log in later for persistent access.
A manipulated account, for example one given new privileges, is usually used soon after.
